title: 3D Garment Surface Textures - Save
content: **Objective** Save all texture images used on Garments and subsidiary Materials to a designated folder. Surface textures can also be cropped to a desired size before they are saved (ver2.5.0). ** Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ **Surface Textures** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ **Surface Textures** → The Save File window appears. 2. Select a Folder location to save the Surface Textures, then press **Save**. → The Save Surface Textures window appears. 3. Select from the available settings. **Original Size** | Saves the surface textures in its original size. ---|--- **Crop Fabric Textures** | Crops the image file based on the value entered. 4. Click **OK**. → The selected image size setting is applied and the files are saved to the Folder location assigned. **※ Note:** Surface textures refers to the surface texture of a Garment.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for saving garment surface texture images to a designated folder, with options for original size or cropping before saving.

title: [Print Layout Mode] Roll Width
content: **List of Contents** Roll Width Roll Width Properties **Roll Width** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P_WA3drM340 \- Adjust the width of the fabric roll in the Print Layout Mode. \- Main Menu ▶ Simulation Mode Button ▶ **PRINT LAYOUT**. **Roll Width Properties** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T1uAioXc-BA \- Select the **Edit Texture** tool from the 3D toolbar. Then, select the Pattern with a texture to be edited. → The selected texture's properties appear in the Property Editor. \- Adjust **Width** and **Position** under the **Roll** option (ver5.0.0.) \- For **Width** , select a preset from the drop-down menu on the right, or insert specific values to either the **in** or **mm** option. \- Change the fabric placement with the **Position** option (ver5.0.0.) → The fabric placement changes based on the inserted values. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on adjusting roll width and its properties in Print Layout Mode, complemented by instructional YouTube videos.

title: Convert to Avatar
content: **List of Contents** Convert to Avatar Load 3D Body File Align 3D Body and CLO Avatar Save Converted Avatar **Convert to Avatar ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EVmOocECOL8 \- Convert 3D dummies or body scans to CLO avatars maintaining their body shapes. \- Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ **Convert to Avatar ** **Load 3D Body file ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Biv28X6TBA4 \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ **Convert to Avatar** \- Load a 3D body file, preferably in attention pose, as a reference for the conversion. \- Select the CLO Avatar to be converted with the 3D body file. \- Click **Next**. **Align 3D Body and CLO Avatar ** * **Change Avatar Pose ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b8fAbFMeGzo - Select the Pose folder corresponding to the loaded Avatar. \- Load attention pose. \- Check **Joint Rotation Only** and select **OK**. * **Align Height and Inseam with Avatar Size Editor ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=adQH_A6I5vg \- Select **Open Avatar Size Editor**. \- Adjust **Height** to align the shoulder height between the CLO Avatar and the 3D body. \- Adjust **Inseam** to align the crotch height between the CLO Avatar and the 3D body. \- Once the adjustment is completed, close the Avatar Size Editor. * **Align Avatar Joints** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yrn7-Ttwy9Q \- Align all joints: total body, ankle, arm, and neck. \- Make sure to align above four locations as closely as possible for more accurate conversion. \- Select **Convert** once all adjustments are completed. **Save Converted Avatar ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oxF61xDL60k \- Rotate to check the quality of the converted avatar. \- Click **Save as Avatar** to save the converted avatar when it's satisfactory. \- When additional modification is needed, click **Back** to repeat previous steps. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for converting 3D body files into CLO avatars, ensuring accurate alignment and saving of the final avatar.

title: Save Image

Click **Save** after choosing the file format (PNG/JPG/PDF), saving path, file name. → The Snapshot window appears. 3. title: Screen Layout
content: **List of Contents** Edit Size Layout Full Screen Reset **Objective** Modify screen layout as needed. **Operation** **Edit Size** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Toolbar ▶**Size Editing Fields ** 2. Insert Height or Width of 3D windows. → 3D windows adjust accordingly. **Layout** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Toolbar ▶ **Layout**** ** 2. Select desired layout option. ** Wrap (Default)** | 3D windows wraps around according to the program's screen size. ---|--- **Horizontal** | 3D windows align horizontally or at the center. ** Vertical** | 3D windows align vertically or at the center. → 3D windows are laid out based on the selected option. **Full Screen** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Toolbar ▶ **Full Screen** → It will enter the full screen mode maintaining the screen layout based on the monitor resolution. 2. title: Flattening as Straight Line
content: ### **Objective** Maintain particular Line (Avatar) straight when flattening a Pattern. **Location ** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Edit 3D Pen (Avatar)** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit_Line.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000520707/Edit_Line.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Avatar)** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Edit 3D Pen****(Avatar)** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit_Line.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000520707/Edit_Line.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Avatar)** → When the Avatar is draped, its Garment becomes translucent. 2. title: Show Style Line
content: ### **Objective ** Express and emphasize style lines, silhouette, internal/external lines, fold lines of 3D Garments. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Show Style Lines (Alt+0)** 3D Window ▶ 3D Garment Display Icon ▶ **Show Style Lines** (ver5.0 or later) **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below:** **Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 3D Garment ▶**Show Style Lines (Alt+0)** 3D Window ▶ 3D Garment Display Icon ▶ **Show Style Lines** (ver5.0 or later)** **→ The Style Line window and Style Lines are now being displayed on the 3D Garment. 2. Set details of the Style Lines. **Thickness** | Sets the thickness of Style Lines. ---|--- **Color** | Sets the color of Style Lines. **Show Silhouette** | Shows or hides the outline of 3D Garment where it meets the background as well as folds and wrinkles (ver2.5.0). → The settings are now being applied to the 3D Garment. **※ Note:** * If wanting to hide particular Internal Shapes and Lines, select it and turn off (uncheck) **Style Lines** option in the Property Editor (ver2.4.0). * Show or hide Style Lines by Pattern or segment. After selecting a Pattern or a segment, navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Select a Segment ▶ **Show Style Lines** and toggle on or off the option (ver5.0.0.)
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to display and customize style lines and silhouettes for 3D garments within the software.

title: Change Pose by OBJ Morphing
content: **Objective** Vertex Morphing has a merit of maintaining avatar's final form without any distortion. However on the other hand, garments may fall off during the morphing process, especially when there is a large difference between the first and the last pose as the pose changes by the minimum distances between points in the avatar rather than the units of avatar joints. Therefore if a big difference between the poses, it is recommended to create an OBJ file for interim pose and morph stage-by-stage. If it is inconvenience, change pose by another method, [Change Pose by Using Collada](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002633147). **Operation** 1. After dressing an avatar in CLO, at least two files are required to change poses such as T-pose avatar and another avatar in desired pose. Export both of the files in OBJ format. To find export method in details, check [3D File (OBJ) Import/Export ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000494107) for the reference. 2. Click File ▶ Import ▶ **OBJ** and select the T-pose OBJ file of the previously exported avatar. Click **OK** on the option dialogue to load the avatar. 3. Put the garments on top of the loaded avatar. 4. Click File ▶ Import ▶ **Morph Target** and load the previously saved avatar with another pose. Set the 'Morphing Frame Count' in the option dialogue, then click **OK**. 5. The **Simulation** button automatically activates and the avatar pose slowly changes according to the set frame count. The garment also starts simulating in accordance with the change. Adjust garments if necessary, after the final pose simulation.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to effectively use Vertex Morphing in CLO to maintain avatar garment integrity during pose transitions.

title: [3D Tool] Free Sewing
content: ### **Objective** In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶**Free Sewing ** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001254128/_______.png) **Free Sewing** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Free Sewing ** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001254128/_______.png) **Free Sewing ** → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Click, drag and double click on Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start and end points of the first half of the seam. 3. Similarly, click again on another Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start point of the second half of the seam. → Drag the mouse cursor as a blue point appears guiding the length of the first half of the seam. 4. The mouse cursor snaps to the blue guide point. 5. Be mindful to make the Directional Notches parallel to each other and click to complete the second half of the seam. **※ Note:** * The face of the Directional Notch of a Sewing Line defers depending on the order of establishing the start and the end point of the Sewing Line. * Right click while establishing the Free Sewing Line to enter the desired length of the Sewing Line in the Create Sewing Line window. * Use the shortcut to establish M:N sewing lines. For more detail, please reference [M:N Free Sewing](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001754668).
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users on how to effectively utilize the Free Sewing feature in 3D design software to create and manage Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes.

title: [3D Tool] 1:N Free Sewing
content: **Objective ** In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶**Free Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001244107/_______.png) **Free Sewing** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Free Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001244107/_______.png) **Free Sewing** → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Establish the start and the end point on the Pattern outline, which is called as 1, where multiple Patterns are sewn to. 3. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. → The Sewing Line appears in neon color. 4. While holding down the Shift key, establish Sewing Lines on N Patterns. Similar to setting regular Free Sewing Lines, be careful with Directional Notches. 5. Release the Shift key to complete. **※ Note** * While establishing N Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Free Sewing feature in Clo3D to create and manage Sewing Lines on pattern outlines and internal shapes in both 2D and 3D views.

title: [3D Tool] 1:N Segment Sewing
content: **Objective** In the 3D window, easily sew multiple segments (N) to a single segment (1.) If the total length of N segments and the length of 1 segment are different, the 1 segment is equally divided by the number of N segments. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶**Segment Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001290728/_______.png) **Segment Sewing** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Segment Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001290728/_______.png) **Segment Sewing** → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Select a single segment which multiple segments are sewn to. 3. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. → The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. 4. While holding down the Shift key on the keyboard, drag the mouse to hover over the N segments. Before clicking the segment, be careful to make Directional Notches parallel to each other. 5. Then, click on the segments to establish Sewing Lines on the N segments. 6. Release the Shift key to complete the 1:N Segment Sewing. **※ Note** * While establishing N Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: The Segment Sewing page provides a straightforward guide for efficiently sewing multiple segments to a single segment in a 3D environment, ensuring seamless integration and alignment.

title: [3D Tool] M:N Free Sewing
content: **Objective** In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns (M) to multiple Patterns (N) at once. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **M:N Free Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005448927/M_N________.png) **M:N Free Sewing** **※ Note:** Hold down the **Free Sewing** tool for a while to access the **M:N Free Sewing** Tool. ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **M:N Free Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005448927/M_N________.png) **M:N Free Sewing** → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Establish Free Sewing Lines on multiple Patterns, which are considered as M Patterns. 3. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. → The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. 4. While being mindful of Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on Patterns which are sewn to M Patterns. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M:N Sewing Lines. → All Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. **※ Note:** * While establishing the Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. * While establishing M:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the Sewing Line cannot be applied. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Discover how to seamlessly create and manage multiple sewing connections between patterns using the M:N Free Sewing tool in our 3D design software.

title: [3D Tool] M:N Segment Sewing
content: **Objective** In the 3D window, easily sew multiple segments (M) to multiple segments (N) at once and edit them as a group. When the total length of multiple segments corresponding to M is different from the total length of multiple segments corresponding to N, N segments are divided in proportion to M segments. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **M:N Segment Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001290748/M_N________.png) **M:N Segment Sewing** **※ Note:** Hold down the **Segment Sewing** tool for a while to access the **M:N Segment Sewing** tool. ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **M:N Segment Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001290748/M_N________.png) **M:N Segment Sewing ** → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Click on the segments belong to M segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M sewing lines. → M sewing lines are highlighted in neon color. 3. As checking the Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on N segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. → The Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. **※ Note:** * While establishing M:N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. * When you click on an inappropriate segment while sewing, the segment appears in red and you cannot establish Sewing Line on the selected segment. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the M:N Segment Sewing tool to efficiently sew and edit multiple segments in 3D, ensuring proportional adjustments between corresponding segments.

title: [Popup] Copy/Paste Tack

Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ **Edit Tack** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001105367/_______.png) **Edit Tack** → The Garment becomes translucent. 2. Right click on the tack to be copied and pasted. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select **Copy** → The selected tack is copied. 4. Access the right-click pop-up menu again on the copied tack. 5. Select**Paste** or **Mirror Paste**. → Preview of the selected tack follows the mouse cursor in 2D and 3D windows. → Any tack outside of the Pattern do not appear in the 3D window. 6. Click the desired location to paste the tack. ** Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ **Edit Tack** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001105367/_______.png) **Edit Tack** → The Garment becomes translucent. 2. title: [Object Browser] Button List Window
content: When creating a button, The Default Button is applied as default setting and displayed in the button list window. Once the Default Button style is modified, it lasts until rerun of the program and it is unable to be deleted.

title: [Tool] Create Buttonholes along Pattern Outline (ver5.1.0)
content: **List of Contents** Create Select Unlink ### **Objective** Create buttonholess along a Pattern Outline in a constant interval and distance. **Location ** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Buttonhole** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Buttonhole** ** Operation** **Create** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Buttonhole** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Buttonhole** 2. Right click on a Pattern Outline. → The **Create Buttons/Buttonholes along Pattern Outline** window appears. **※Note:** To select multiple lines, press down the Shift key and click the lines to be selected. 3. Configure below options as needed: **Start Position** | Distance | Set the distance between the buttonholes and the selected line. ---|---|--- Interval | Set the distance between the buttonholes and the Pattern Outline. Reverse | The direction of which buttonholes are created is reversed to the Start Point. ** Replicate ** | Interval | Adjust the distance between the buttonholes. Number of Button/Buttonholes | Adjust the number of buttonholes to be created. 4. Click **OK**. → Buttonholes are created as a group. **Select** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Buttonhole** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Buttonhole** 2. Click on a buttonhole or a Pattern Outline where buttonholes are created. → All buttonholes in a group are selected. **※Note:** Click again while the group of buttonholes are selected to select a single buttonhole. 3. Change selected buttonholes' [properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002382548) or [style](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000717067-Buttonhole-Style-Properties) or use [right-click pop-up menu](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001042867). → Any changes made are applied to all buttonholes in the same group. → Group information cannot be copied or duplicated. **※Note:** Grouped buttonholes cannot be moved. **Unlink** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Select/Move Button** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Select/Move Button** 2. Right click on the buttonholes or the Pattern Outline and select **Unlink Buttons/Buttonholes**. → The link between the buttonholes are removed. ** ** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for creating, selecting, and unlinking buttonholes along a pattern outline in a design software, ensuring users can efficiently customize their projects.

title: [Popup] Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern
content: ### **Objective** Duplicate buttons as buttonholes, or buttonholes as buttons, to its Symmetric Pattern. **Location ** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Select/Move Button** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015218607/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png) **Select/Move Button** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Select/Move Button** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015218607/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png) **Select/Move Button** 2. Click on the button or buttonhole to be duplicated to its Symmetric Pattern. → The selected button or buttonhole is highlighted in yellow. 3. Right click on the selected button or buttonhole. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 4. Depending on the selected item, select **Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern** or **Duplicate as Buttonhole to Symmetric Pattern**. → The selected button or buttonhole is duplicated as a buttonhole or button, depending on the selected item, to its Symmetric Pattern.
content_description: This web page guides users on how to duplicate buttons and buttonholes in a symmetric pattern using the 3D Toolbar in the design software.

title: [Style Property] Edit Puckering Style Properties
content: **List of Contents** Puckering Style Setting Default Puckering Style **Objective** Edit or reset Puckering style properties. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Puckering Tab ** Operation ** **Puckering Style Setting** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Puckering Tab 2. Click on Puckering style. → Puckering style properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Adjust the properties as needed. **Name** | Name the Puckering style. ---|--- **Material** | Five presets are provided: Cotton, Denim, Leather, Nylon, Polyester. **Texture (ver.5.1.0)** | Apply the texture. **Desaturation** | Maintain the texture of images or patterns while changing colors. **Shadow Intensity** | Adjust the intensity of the texture's shadow. **Shadow Brightness** | Adjust the brightness of the texture's shadow while maintaining the image's pattern and texture. **Normal Map** | Change the Puckering's shape by importing a Normal Map. **Opacity (%)** | Adjust the Normal Map's opacity. **Specification** | **Density (%)** | Adjust the density of the Normal Map. **Width (mm)** | Adjust the width of the Normal Map. **Default Puckering Style** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Puckering Tab 2. Right click on the puckering style to make as a default, and click **Reset**. → The selected puckering style's properties are reset to the Default Puckering's. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for editing and resetting puckering style properties in the Object Browser's Puckering Tab.

title: Connection to DMIx Cloud & Compatible with Material (ver 6.0)
content: **Objective** Simply drag and drop to apply color or AxF files for CLO. Find a variety of digitalized materials & colors from DMIx Cloud Web of Color Digital. **** **Operation** 1. Drag and drop AxF files into the 3D/ 2D window of CLO from the DMIx Cloud webpage. → The AxF files are downloaded in DMIx Download Manager. 2. Drag and drop AxF files to the 3D garment/ 2D Patterns or Click '**Assign to Selected Fabric** ' in **DMIx Download Manager** once you selected 3D garment/2D patterns. → AxF file is applied. **※ Note: ** * Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Clicking **DMIx Download Manager** also allows you to execute the window. * New items are added when you drag and drop the AxF file of **DMIx Download Manager** to the **Fabric** **List**.
content_description: Easily enhance your CLO designs by dragging and dropping color or AxF files from DMIx Cloud to apply a diverse range of digital materials.
